title: Close the seconds hole in the duration law and retoken the one raw 1.1s
body:
## Summary
design/check-tokens.mjs bans raw `px` and `ms` but not `s`, so a duration written in seconds passes lint; one already has: `animation: al-pulse 1.1s` in examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/lanes.css:650.

## Description
DESIGN.md §7 says "one clock, in tokens.css, and no JavaScript in this app types a millisecond", and `pnpm --filter atlas lint` enforces it through check-tokens' RAW regex `/(?<![\w-])(\d*\.?\d+)(px|ms)\b/g` (examples/atlas/design/check-tokens.mjs:48). The unit `s` is not in the alternation, so `0.2s` or `1.1s` is invisible to the gate (quality-gates/unparseable-form-is-a-finding: the same value written another way evades a source-pattern check; design-tokens/token-enforcement). A scan of app/, components/ and lib/ with `s` added finds exactly one hit, the lanes drawing's pulse at examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/lanes.css:650, a raw 1.1 s duration outside the five-token clock. Fixed means: RAW matches `px|ms|s`, the lanes pulse reads a declared `--at-dur-*` or `--al-*` token, and test/check-tokens.test.ts gains a seeded `0.2s` case.

## Flow
- seed `transition: opacity 0.2s` in any atlas stylesheet -> `pnpm --filter atlas lint` -> exit 0 today
- fix: give the pulse a duration token in the lanes context's stylesheet (or tokens.css), then add `s` to RAW in check-tokens.mjs
- add a seeded-seconds case to test/check-tokens.test.ts, watch it fail before the regex change and pass after

## Expected impact
A reader of DESIGN.md can trust that every duration is on the clock; reduced-motion and the Calm-style zeroing reach every animation. Could break: lint goes red the moment the regex lands unless lanes.css:650 is retokened first, which is why it is out of this round's write set.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every duration in the app is a clock token, as DESIGN.md §7 states
Before: raw durations in seconds that pass lint: 1 (lanes.css:650); seeded `0.2s` passes the gate
After: predicted 0 and the seeded case exits 1; not taken - the one hit is in the lanes context's file, which this round may not edit, and the regex alone would turn lint red
Method: probe - the extended regex run over app/, components/, lib/ found the one hit; the fix needs a file another agent owns this wave
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a seeded `0.2s` case in examples/atlas/test/check-tokens.test.ts (red before the regex change, green after), plus `pnpm --filter atlas lint` green with lanes.css:650 retokened

title: The lanes node and lib.rs still describe the module bar the model no longer has
body:
## Summary
After ead62ed the model says Main is one scene with depths and the companion is her own window, but the lanes drawing's node still reads "module bar · panel" (examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/workflow.ts:188,191) and lib.rs's own docstring still says module-first (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:4).

## Description
ADR 0095 deleted the module bar and the module registry; README §3.5 reads "one scene with depths". This round brought data/ in line (concept D-3, S-02, C-008, C-009, lib.rs's sentence, four edges). Two other renderings of the same rule were outside the write set: the lanes node that carries sys-shell/sys-panel (workflow.ts:188 sublabel "module bar · panel", :191 note "The Tauri window, the module bar and the panel in it") and the shell's module docstring (lib.rs:4-6: "The window is module-first ... a thin bar, the selected module at full width"). A reader of the drawing now sees one claim at L0 and the opposite in the L2 pane (docs-sync/coupled-surface-inventory). Fixed means: the lanes node sublabel and note name the console and her window, and lib.rs's docstring names ADR 0026/0087/0088.

## Flow
- open Atlas -> L0 lanes node for the shell reads "module bar · panel"
- open its component -> L2 pane reads "Two windows, one product ... Rust owns every rectangle" (data/components.ts)
- fix: reword workflow.ts:188,191 in the lanes context, and lib.rs:4-6 in the desktop shell context

## Expected impact
The drawing stops contradicting its own pane; an agent's read_view and the sheet agree. Could break: a lanes test that pins the sublabel text, if one exists.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one description of the window across the model, the drawing and the shell
Before: phrases naming the deleted bar outside data/: 3 (workflow.ts:188, workflow.ts:191, lib.rs:4)
After: predicted 0; not taken - both files belong to contexts this round does not own
Method: probe - grep for "module bar|module-first" over examples/atlas/components and apps/desktop/src-tauri/src
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/workflow.ts:188  sublabel: "module bar · panel",
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/workflow.ts:191  note: "The Tauri window, the module bar and the panel in it, ..."
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:4  //! rectangle. The window is module-first (README section 3.5): a thin bar, the selected module at
docs/adr/0095-...md: "Deleted: ModuleBar, the app root, the module registry"
instrument: grep count of "module bar|module-first" in examples/atlas/components and apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs: 3 -> 0, with atlas lint/test and cargo check green

title: Model the halo and the nebius engine README 3.1 now names
body:
## Summary
README §3.1 lists the halo (ADR 0027) under surfaces and an API engine (`nebius`, ADR 0031) under harness; Atlas, which says it does not paraphrase §3.1, has no component for either and its layer blurbs stop before them (examples/atlas/data/systems.ts:21-22, :46-47).

## Description
data/systems.ts says the layer blurbs are "README §3.1's own words ... kept verbatim where they fit". README.md:136-141 now reads "... a voice client, the halo (screen-edge light, ADR 0027)" and "... an API engine (`nebius`, Nemotron on Token Factory) behind the `ModelFn` port (ADR 0031)". Neither the halo (apps/desktop/src/halo, apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/halo.rs) nor the nebius engine (src/athena/harness) is a component, so the lens for act 1 or invariant 5 cannot light them and an agent's read_model says the harness is CLI-only. Fixed means: two components (halo under sys-shell, the API engine under sys-runner), their edges and ADRs (27, 31), and the two blurbs extended. Sized as B because the app's README, DESIGN.md and the lanes code comments print "sixty-eight components" as prose in files outside this context, and the lanes node sublabels may want the new parts.

## Flow
- read README.md §3.1 -> halo and nebius are named
- call read_model / open S-01 or S-10 in Atlas -> neither appears
- fix: add C-069 halo and C-070 the API engine with citations; extend the two blurbs; re-run data.test (citations) and the lanes tests

## Expected impact
The atlas maps the machine README describes, not the one of a month ago. Could break: prose counts ("sixty-eight") in README/DESIGN/lanes comments go stale and need the same commit.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every part README §3.1 names has a component in the model
Before: README §3.1 parts with no component: 2 (halo, nebius engine)
After: predicted 0; not taken - the coupled prose and lanes copy are in other contexts' files
Method: simulation - README.md:136-141 read against data/components.ts; no instrument run because the coupled surfaces are out of scope
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
README.md:137  other agents over MCP, a voice client, the halo (screen-edge light, ADR 0027)
README.md:140-141  structural policy, the OP grammar, engine probes; an API engine (`nebius`, ...) behind the `ModelFn` port (ADR 0031)
examples/atlas/data/systems.ts:21-22  blurb ends "... other agents over MCP, a voice client"
grep -c "halo\|nebius" examples/atlas/data/*.ts -> 0
instrument: a data.test case asserting every `ADR NNNN` named in README §3.1's layer block is cited by some component, plus the citation case already in test/data.test.ts

title: Atlas declares APP_ID but never publishes athena:app, unlike ledgerbox
body:
## Summary
examples/atlas/lib/constants.ts:11-12 declares APP_ID and APP_VERSION with zero consumers, and app/layout.tsx publishes no `athena:app` meta, so Athena catalogs Atlas under its web origin; ledgerbox publishes its id (examples/ledgerbox/app/layout.tsx:11).

## Description
README §3.4: a page's origin is "`host:<app_id>`: the page's published `athena:app`, else the id derived from its web origin" (ADR 0065). Ledgerbox sets `other: { "athena:app": "ledgerbox", "athena:app-version": "0.1.0" }` with the comment "App identity for a WebMCP consumer"; Atlas carries the same two constants and uses neither (zero-consumer grep below), so the identity it declares is never said. Hirelane and tidycrm also publish nothing, where APP_ID is consumed by db.ts. Fixed means one of: publish `athena:app` from APP_ID/APP_VERSION in app/layout.tsx (and decide the same for hirelane/tidycrm), or delete the two dead constants. Publishing changes the origin key Athena's trust rows are filed under (ADR 0100), so it is a studio-wide identity call, not a local cleanup.

## Flow
- open Atlas in the shell -> the relay reads no `athena:app` -> the app is `host:web_...` from its origin
- open ledgerbox -> `host:ledgerbox`
- fix: either publish from APP_ID in layout metadata (one line) with a test, or remove the unused constants

## Expected impact
Atlas's identity in the origins table and on decision cards matches the name it declares. Could break: an existing trust row filed under the origin-derived id stops matching.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a declared app identity is either published or not declared
Before: consumers of APP_ID/APP_VERSION in examples/atlas: 0; example apps publishing athena:app: 1 of 4
After: predicted consumers 1 (layout metadata) or the constants gone; not taken - changes the key trust is filed under
Method: probe - grep for APP_ID, APP_VERSION and athena:app across examples/
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
grep -rn "APP_ID\|APP_VERSION" examples/atlas --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx -> only examples/atlas/lib/constants.ts:11,12
grep -rn "athena:app" examples/*/app -> examples/ledgerbox/app/layout.tsx:11 only
README.md §3.4 tier table: origin is the page's published athena:app, else derived from its web origin (ADR 0065)
instrument: a layout metadata test (or a journey-free relay probe) asserting `athena:app` equals APP_ID, and a check of the daemon's origins rows for the atlas origin before and after

title: A render error in Atlas falls to Next's default unstyled error page
body:
## Summary
examples/atlas/app/ has no error.tsx or global-error.tsx, so an exception anywhere in the one client tree (components/atlas/Atlas.tsx) replaces the whole dark blueprint with Next's default "Application error" page.

## Description
app/page.tsx renders one client component, and every surface (the drawing, the pane, the tools) lives under it. Nothing in app/ catches a render error, so a throw in a variant (e.g. the runtime-unsafe `?variant=` capture useChoice.ts documents at examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/useChoice.ts:18-27) shows the framework's light default page on a dark-only app (globals.css sets `color-scheme: dark`). state-coverage asks what shows when the source FAILS; today that state was never designed. No example app has an error boundary, so the fix is either local (an app/error.tsx in the blueprint tokens with a reload action) or a kit primitive the studio shares.

## Flow
- force a throw inside a variant render -> Next's default error screen, unstyled, no way back but reload
- fix: app/error.tsx (client) drawn in --at-* tokens, naming the failure and offering reset(); or a demo-kit boundary all four apps mount

## Expected impact
A failing drawing degrades to a page in the app's own design with a retry, instead of a blank framework screen. Could break: nothing at rest; the boundary only renders on error.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the failure state of the one client tree is designed
Before: error boundaries in examples/*/app: 0 (find app -name 'error.tsx' over the four apps)
After: predicted 1 for atlas (or 4 via the kit); not taken - showing it needs a DOM render or a browser
Method: simulation - no DOM renderer in this package's node --test; the instrument is a render test or a browser run
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a render test (react-dom/server or a DOM test env) that throws inside the tree and asserts the boundary's text and reset control, or one browser run against `next dev`
